title: Copilot Studio: conversational configuration of connectors with in-chat sign-in
notes: claim 69: severity blocker on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: The risk rationale presents consent bypass as confirmed governance of the connection prompt, although the body correctly says that relationship is unconfirmed. The briefing also incorrectly says blocked tools disappear and omits the environment-group restriction that can prevent changes to environment credit controls.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Data policies govern connector tools for Copilot Studio agents in environments included in the policy scope.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A data-policy-blocked tool cannot be selected by a maker or used by an agent.
claims.quote: When a data policy blocks a tool, the tool appears unavailable in the Add a tool panel and you can't select it.

claims.claim: Blocking a connector removes it from the maker's Add a tool list.
claims.quote: When a data policy blocks a tool, the tool appears unavailable in the Add a tool panel and you can't select it.
claims.fix: Replace 'Data policies that block a connector remove it from the maker's Add a tool list' with 'A tool blocked by a data policy appears unavailable in the maker's Add a tool panel and cannot be selected'.

claims.claim: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks tools in connected MCP servers that rely on those connectors.
claims.quote: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.claim: Makers and users see error messages for data policy violations.
claims.quote: Agent makers and users see error messages for any data policy violation.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Control maker credential options lets administrators allow maker credentials, end-user credentials or both for agent tools.
claims.quote: You choose whether makers can select to use their own credentials for authenticating tool connections, to use the end-user's credentials, or to have access to both.

claims.claim: Both End-user and Maker-provided credential options are enabled by default.
claims.quote: By default, both End-user and Maker-provided credentials are enabled.

claims.claim: Turning either credential option off immediately changes all tools for all agents in the affected environments.
claims.quote: Searched: Control maker credential options disable End-user all tools. Read configure-no-maker-authentication and its search excerpts. The immediate all-tools warning describes disabling maker credentials, not either option.
claims.fix: Replace 'turning one off immediately changes all tools for all agents in the affected environments' with 'preventing maker-provided credentials changes all tools for all agents in the affected environments to require end-user credentials at runtime'. This is the warning at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/configure-no-maker-authentication.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness agents use consumption-based billing measured in Copilot Credits for building, testing and running.
claims.quote: Agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness use consumption-based billing. Building, testing, evaluating, and running these agents can consume Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness usage is not included with a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: This usage isn't included with a user's Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing: Meter
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing starts when building starts.
claims.quote: Unlike the standard harness, which starts billing after publish, the Microsoft Copilot harness charges credits from the moment you start building.

claims.claim: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs, from prepaid capacity or through the environment's pay-as-you-go billing plan, and not to the individual makers or users who run agents.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: No credit rate specific to connection setup through chat was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio connectors in-chat sign-in licensing credits rate. Read billing-credit-overview and search excerpts from requirements-messages-management and billing-licensing; published activity rates do not name a separate connection-setup rate.

claims.claim: The variable cost rating names the documented Copilot Credits meter.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: The environment tenant-capacity draw control is at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Licensing. Under Products, select Copilot Studio. Select Manage Copilot Credits. Select the environment. ... Under Capacity overages, clear Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes environment credit allocations and the TenantPool enforcement rule.
claims.quote: $apiBaseUrl = "https://api.powerplatform.com"; $apiVersion = "2024-10-01"; Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"; @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false }
claims.fix: Keep the call unchanged; the deterministic missing-endpoint lead is a false positive caused by variables in the example. Replace 'The request body sets the TenantPool enforcement rule' with 'The request body sets allocatedEntitlements[].allocation.quantity and allocatedEntitlements[].enforcementRules, using ruleType TenantPool and enabled to control tenant-capacity draw'.

claims.claim: Capacity management requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent role that manages licensing and capacity.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot Studio capacity, you need the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: Capacity and consumption controls apply across Copilot Studio and can affect other agents, workflows and features in an environment.
claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. They aren't exclusive to the Microsoft Copilot harness. Configure controls with the other Copilot Studio agents, workflows, and features in mind for each environment.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Spend controls; Governance controls
claims.claim: Clearing tenant-capacity draw does not prevent continued consumption through a linked pay-as-you-go Azure subscription.
claims.quote: If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.

claims.claim: An agent monthly limit is configured at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Copilot Studio > Manage Agents > agent > Set limit.
claims.quote: In the Power Platform admin center, go to Licensing > Copilot Studio. Select Manage Agents. Select the agent, and then select Set limit. Enter the monthly Copilot Credit limit.

claims.claim: Stop usage can turn an agent off when it reaches its monthly limit.
claims.quote: Turn on Stop usage if the agent should be turned off when it reaches the limit.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center Licensing > Copilot Studio pages provide environment and agent credit consumption views.
claims.quote: Use the Copilot Studio licensing pages in the Power Platform admin center to review consumption at multiple levels: ... Environment: Compare prepaid and pay-as-you-go consumption ... Agent: Review month-to-date billed credits, configured limits, and agent status.

claims.claim: The connector-blocking path is Power Platform admin center > Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Assign connectors > connector > Block.
claims.quote: Select Next. The Add an environment page appears. ... Select Next. The Assign connectors page appears. ... Select the three dots next to the connector ... select Block.
claims.fix: Expand the path to 'Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Add an environment > Assign connectors > connector > three dots > Block' in front matter and the rendered table. These omissions are an environment-selection step and an unlabelled menu button, not blockers under the verifier's path rule.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy GUID> -Classification Blocked -Connectors $connectors moves the specified connectors into the policy's Blocked group.
claims.quote: The name of the group to which the connectors should be added. Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.claim: Data policy prerequisites name a tenant admin or the Environment Admin role.
claims.quote: Be a tenant admin or have the Environment Admin role.

claims.claim: No admin UI path for changing per-agent connector consent bypass was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio connector consent bypass admin center UI Connection Required. Opened admin-connector-consent-bypass and pac copilot-studio; both document automation, not an admin UI for changing this setting.

claims.claim: Set-AdminCopilotStudioBotConnectorConsentBypass -EnvironmentId <environment ID> -BotId <agent ID> -BypassConsent $false restores normal connector consent-card behaviour.
claims.quote: Use $false to restore the normal consent-card behavior: Set-AdminCopilotStudioBotConnectorConsentBypass -EnvironmentId "7d91e4b2-a638-4f0c-b527-9e6a13d8c045" -BotId "e6b4c2a9-17f3-48d5-8c01-2a9f7e63b4d8" -BypassConsent $false

claims.claim: The consent-bypass PowerShell functions come from the provided script and require the documented Entra application setup.
claims.quote: The ConsentBypass-CopilotStudio.ps1 script is available on the computer that runs the commands. ... A single-tenant Microsoft Entra application is configured for interactive authentication.

claims.claim: The consent-bypass application requires the CopilotStudio.AdminActions.Invoke delegated Power Platform API permission.
claims.quote: The application has the CopilotStudio.AdminActions.Invoke delegated Power Platform API permission.

claims.claim: Power Platform Administrator is the least-privilege of the three roles supported for the consent-bypass commands.
claims.quote: The signed-in account has one of these Microsoft Entra roles: Power Platform Administrator (least privilege of the listed roles); AI Administrator; Global Administrator.

claims.claim: Setting BypassConsent to $true bypasses connector consent cards.
claims.quote: Step 8: Turn on consent bypass ... Set-AdminCopilotStudioBotConnectorConsentBypass ... -BypassConsent $true

claims.claim: Get-AdminCopilotStudioBotConnectorConsentBypass reads whether an agent's connector consent cards are bypassed.
claims.quote: This command only reads the setting. It doesn't change the setting. ... The returned AdminConsentBypass value indicates the current state: True: Consent cards are bypassed. False: Consent cards are shown.

claims.claim: The Power Platform CLI also documents the preview command pac copilot-studio set-connector-consent-bypass.
claims.quote: pac copilot-studio set-connector-consent-bypass ... (Preview) Set the admin connector consent bypass setting for a bot.

claims.claim: Dataverse for Teams environments do not support agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness.
claims.quote: Dataverse for Teams environments don't support agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness.

claims.claim: The risk rationale says per-agent consent settings cover these in-chat connection prompts, despite the body saying that applicability is unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Rationale: 'Data policies and per-agent consent settings cover this'. Body: 'Microsoft does not say whether the Connection Required card is one of those consent cards, so confirm before relying on it.'
claims.fix: Replace 'Data policies and per-agent consent settings cover this, but makers and users need guidance on the prompts' with 'Data policies govern connector tools; whether consent bypass affects the Connection Required card is not confirmed, and makers and users need guidance on the documented prompts'.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Spend controls; controls[0].note; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Administrators can clear tenant-capacity draw for an environment or set it through the allocation API, without a stated environment-group exception.
claims.quote: If a published environment group rule governs Draw from the available capacity in my tenant, you can't override the setting for an individual environment.
claims.fix: Qualify the environment-level instructions and controls[0].note with: 'If a published environment-group rule governs this option, the environment setting cannot be overridden and API updates return TenantPoolLockedByPolicy. Change and republish the group rule, or remove the environment from the group to manage the setting independently.' The restriction is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/programmability-tutorial-manage-copilot-credit-allocations.
